original_question: Classify all null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 11: "Study and classify null 2-type submanifolds. In particular, classify all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem targeted by the paper, including the two emphasized special cases: null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional Euclidean space and in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces. It is essentially Problem 11 verbatim, except that the paper says "Study and classify" and relies on earlier sections for the precise meaning of "null 2-type."
missing_details: The paper’s general classification problem is posed in the Euclidean finite-type setting; the pseudo-Euclidean extension is singled out only in the particular 4-dimensional surface case, not as a full parallel general problem.

“Null 2-type” should be defined via the spectral decomposition of the position vector field: x = c + x1 + x2, where c is constant, x1 and x2 are nonconstant, Δx1 = 0, and Δx2 = λx2 for some nonzero real constant λ.
Δ is the Laplace-Beltrami operator of the induced metric on the immersed manifold.
The underlying setup in the preliminaries is an isometric immersion x: M → E^m of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean space.
Null k-type submanifolds are automatically noncompact; the problem does not impose compactness.

The nearby context gives the necessary consequence ΔH = λH for null 2-type submanifolds, but the paper does not present the classification problem as an equivalent classification of all submanifolds satisfying that PDE, so the question should not be rewritten that way.
refined_question: Let x: M → E^m be an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean m-space, and call M null 2-type if its position vector field admits a spectral decomposition x = c + x1 + x2 with c constant, x1 and x2 nonconstant, Δx1 = 0, and Δx2 = λx2 for some nonzero real constant λ, where Δ is the Laplace-Beltrami operator of the induced metric. Study and classify all such null 2-type submanifolds of Euclidean spaces. In particular, determine all null 2-type surfaces in E^4 and, in the analogous pseudo-Euclidean setting, all null 2-type surfaces in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean spaces.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: in arXiv:1307.6582 the relevant target is Section 6, Problem 11. To make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, the refined version restores the exact finite-type setup from the preliminaries: the immersion framework, the role of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, and the spectral definition of null 2-type. I also kept the pseudo-Euclidean clause only in the special 4-dimensional surface case, because that is exactly how the paper states the problem. I did not replace the question by a PDE-only version using ΔH = λH, since the paper presents that equation only as a consequence/nearby characterization context, not as an explicitly equivalent reformulation of Problem 11.
